library(dplyr)
library(Matrix)
library(reshape)
library(plyr)

#Linear mixed effect model on 1st harvest data
Harv1Individuals<-read.csv ("../data/1stHarvRformatedSeeds_Nov27.csv")

Harv1Individuals$City<-as.factor(Harv1Individuals$City)
#head(Harv1Individuals)

# CREATING Fecundity variable- Fruit count combined with seed count ---------------------------

Harv1Individuals$Fecundity<-Harv1Individuals$Seed_count/5 * Harv1Individuals$N_Fruits

# Bushiness- Branch count and height --------------------------------------
#Scaling phenotypes to have a mean of zero and a std deviation of 1.

Harv1Individuals<-Harv1Individuals %>%
  mutate_at(c("HavHeight_Scaled", "Rosbranches_Scaled", "Caulibranches_Scaled"), ~(scale(.)%>%as.vector))

#RosetteSTD<-Harv1Individuals$Rosbranches_Scaled
#CaulineSTD<-Harv1Individuals$Caulibranches_Scaled
#Height_HarvSTD<-Harv1Individuals$HavHeight_Scaled


#Clculating a bushyness score= Having them all equally weighted below at 0.5 but could put more weight on rosette branch if
#we think this is the driving factor for bushiess. 
#The below code suggests that rosette branches are positively correlated with bushiness
#and that cauline branches and height are negatively correlated with bushiness. 

#This code is done without normalising the variables.

#Changed weight for rosette branches to carry more weight as I fell this is the most defining factor.

#data_Bushiness<-PhenotypesScaled %>% 
# mutate(BushinessScore = (0.5 * RosetteSTD) - (0.5 * CaulineSTD)-(0.5 * Height_HarvSTD))

Harv1Individuals$BushyScore = Harv1Individuals$Rosbranches_Scaled/2 - Harv1Individuals$Caulibranches_Scaled/2 - Harv1Individuals$HavHeight_Scaled/2

  abs(x-mean(x,na.rm=TRUE)) > 3.0*sd(x,na.rm=TRUE)

  abs(x-mean(x,na.rm=TRUE))/sd(x,na.rm=TRUE)
}

# Creating bushiness variable ---------------------------------------------
#install.packages("dplyr")
library(dplyr)
#Scaling phenotypes to have a mean of zero and a std deviation of 1.

BranchHeightScaled<-Harv1GCMidWestInd %>%
  mutate_at(c("Height_Harvest", "Rosette_branches", "Cauline_branches"), ~(scale(.)%>%as.vector))

BranchHeightScaled


RosetteSTD<-BranchHeightScaled$Rosette_branches
CaulineSTD<-BranchHeightScaled$Cauline_branches
Height_HarvSTD<-BranchHeightScaled$Height_Harvest

head(RosetteSTD)

#Clculating a bushyness score= Having them all equally weighted below at 0.5 but could put more weight on rosette branch if
#we think this is the driving factor for bushiess. 
#The below code suggests that rosette branches are positively correlated with bushiness
#and that cauline branches and height are negatively correlated with bushiness. 

#This code is done without normalising the variables.

#Changed weight for rosette branches to carry more weight as I fell this is the most defining factor.

#data_Bushiness<-PhenotypesScaled %>% 
 # mutate(BushinessScore = (0.5 * RosetteSTD) - (0.5 * CaulineSTD)-(0.5 * Height_HarvSTD))

BranchHeightScaled$BushinessScore = (0.5 * RosetteSTD) - (0.5 * CaulineSTD)-(0.5 * Height_HarvSTD)

head(BranchHeightScaled)
str(BranchHeightScaled)
data$City<-as.factor(data_Bushiness$City)

#Determining if this trait is normally distributed
BushinessScore<-ggplot(BranchHeightScaled, aes(BushinessScore)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill='lightgray', col='black') +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean=mean(Harv1GCMidWestInd$BushinessScore), sd=sd(Harv1GCMidWestInd$BushinessScore)),
                col='red', lwd=2, lty='dashed')
BushinessScore

#Histogram a little right skewed but not bad.

qqnorm(BranchHeightScaled$BushinessScore, main='Normal')
qqline(BranchHeightScaled$BushinessScore)
#Relatively normal

#install.packages("car")
#library(car)
leveneTest(BushinessScore ~ City, data = BranchHeightScaled)
#not sig.

#install.packages("moments")

skewness(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Height_Flower, na.rm = TRUE)

Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FH = sqrt(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Height_Flower)

Tsqrt_FH<-ggplot(Harv1GCMidWestInd, aes(Tsqrt_FH)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill='lightgray', col='black') +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean=mean(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FH), sd=sd(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FH)),
                col='red', lwd=2, lty='dashed')
Tsqrt_FH

#Histogram doesnt quite look normal enough but qqplot looks pretty normal
qqnorm(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FH, main='Normal')
qqline(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FH)

#install.packages("car")
library(car)
leveneTest(Tsqrt_FH ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)

########################

#Log transforming

  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill='lightgray', col='black') +

                col='red', lwd=2, lty='dashed')
TlogFH

#Histogram looks normal
qqnorm(Harv1GCMidWestInd$TlogFH, main='Normal')
qqline(Harv1GCMidWestInd$TlogFH)
#qqplot looks normal- although should check residuals!

leveneTest(TlogFH ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)
#BUT levenes test is now a lot more sig
leveneTest(TlogFH ~ ParentGrowingConditions, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)

####################

#Checking residuals on raw data

FH_Resid <- aov(Height_Flower ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)
summary(FH_Resid)

residuals <- FH_Resid$residuals

qqline(residuals)

#Checking residuals on log transformed data
FH_Resid_log <- aov(TlogFH ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)

#Raw data is not sig for Anova, logged data is sig- but lavenes also more sig :/

residuals <- FH_Resid_log$residuals
qqnorm(residuals)
qqline(residuals)

#jUST NOTING HERE BOTH THE RAW AND LOGGED DATA SHOW SOME SIGNIFICANCE for mixed effect model.

# Creating days to flowering phenotype and analysing that instead  --------
str(Harv1GCMidWestInd)

Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime<-Harv1GCMidWestInd$DaysPlantToBolt + Harv1GCMidWestInd$DaysBoltToFlower
head(Harv1GCMidWestInd)

#Height_Flower
FlowerTime<-ggplot(Harv1GCMidWestInd, aes(FlowerTime)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill='lightgray', col='black') +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean=mean(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime), sd=sd(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime)),
                col='red', lwd=2, lty='dashed')
FlowerTime

#Tail on the right
qqnorm(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime, main='Normal')
qqline(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime)
#Not normal

#install.packages("car")
#library(car)
leveneTest(FlowerTime ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)
#small F value at 2.422, but technically sig at p = 0,04999

leveneTest(FlowerTime ~ ParentGrowingConditions, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)


# Transforming flowering time ---------------------------------------------

mean(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime, na.rm = TRUE)
#36.33

var(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime, na.rm = TRUE)
#192.29

#Variance is greater than the mean, therefore we have overdispersed count data
#And should use a negative binomial regression- i.e. glm.nb. 

#Trying a right trail transformation first to see if can analyse normally. 

#Negative values mean negatively skewed
#Positive values mean positively Skewed- tail on the right
library(moments)
skewness(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime, na.rm = TRUE)
#1.50

#Square-root transfomation for moderate skew
#sqrt(x) for positively skewed data,

str(Harv1GCMidWestInd)

Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FT = sqrt(Harv1GCMidWestInd$FlowerTime)

Tsqrt_FT<-ggplot(Harv1GCMidWestInd, aes(Tsqrt_FT)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill='lightgray', col='black') +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean=mean(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FT), sd=sd(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FT)),
                col='red', lwd=2, lty='dashed')
Tsqrt_FT

#Histogram looks better but not normal
qqnorm(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FT, main='Normal')
qqline(Harv1GCMidWestInd$Tsqrt_FT)

#install.packages("car")
library(car)
leveneTest(Tsqrt_FT ~ City, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)
#F = 6.09, P = 0.0001
leveneTest(Tsqrt_FT ~ ParentGrowingConditions, data = Harv1GCMidWestInd)
#F=8.20, P = 0.0004

# FDR correction on P values ----------------------------------------------


#FDR adjusted P values

P_Table1 <- c(0.0113, 0.0242, 0.0096, 0.5376, 0.4884, 0.3802, 0.0121)

fdr_P_Table1 <- p.adjust(P_Table1, method = "BH")
print(fdr_P_Table1)

#FDR adjusted P values FOR -2 LOG LIKLIHOOD MODELS mean
P_Table2 <- c(0.012, 0.038, 0.009, 0.944, 0.916, 0.822, 0.014)
fdr_P_Table2 <- p.adjust(P_Table1, method = "BH")
print(fdr_P_Table2)

#For the calculated P value
GxE_P_Calculated <- c(0.8390, 0.6393, 0.6536, 0.8911, 0.4718, 0.7394, 0.0931)

fdr_P_GxE <- p.adjust(GxE_P_Calculated, method = "BH")
print(fdr_P_GxE)

#For the model P value
GxE_P_Model <- c(0.582, 0.281, 0.298, 0.689, 0.570, 0.410, 0.003)
fdr_P_GxE_Model <- p.adjust(GxE_P_Model, method = "BH")
print(fdr_P_GxE_Model)
